topics.title: Kailasa Temple, Ellora
topics.fact: The Kailasa Temple at Ellora was carved top-down from a single rock — around 200,000 tonnes of stone removed by hand, with no bricks and nothing assembled.

topics.title: Brihadeeswarar Temple, Thanjavur
topics.fact: The Cholas raised the 66m Brihadeeswarar Temple in 1010 CE; its granite capstone alone weighs roughly 80 tonnes.

topics.title: Konark Sun Temple
topics.fact: Konark's Sun Temple is a colossal stone chariot; its 24 carved wheels double as working sundials.

topics.title: Vittala Temple, Hampi
topics.fact: Hampi's Vittala Temple has stone pillars that ring with musical notes when struck.

topics.title: Chand Baori Stepwell
topics.fact: Chand Baori descends 13 storeys through 3,500 steps arranged in near-perfect geometric symmetry.

topics.title: Rani ki Vav
topics.fact: Rani ki Vav is an inverted underground temple-stepwell with over 500 sculptures — printed on the Indian 100-rupee note.

topics.title: Khajuraho Temples
topics.fact: The Chandelas built the Khajuraho temples in about 200 years; the jungle then hid them for centuries.

topics.title: Meenakshi Temple, Madurai
topics.fact: Madurai's Meenakshi Temple has 14 towering gopurams covered in an estimated 33,000 sculptures.

topics.title: Dilwara Temples, Mount Abu
topics.fact: The Dilwara Jain temples look plain outside, but inside, the marble is carved so finely it turns translucent.

topics.title: Lingaraja Temple, Bhubaneswar
topics.fact: Bhubaneswar's 11th-century Lingaraja Temple rises about 55m in the classic Kalinga style, built without mortar.

topics.title: Virupaksha Temple, Hampi
topics.fact: Hampi's Virupaksha Temple has been in continuous worship since at least the 7th century — over 1,300 years.

topics.title: Modhera Sun Temple
topics.fact: The Solankis built Modhera's Sun Temple in 1027 CE so that the rising equinox sun lights up the inner sanctum.

topics.title: Adalaj Stepwell
topics.fact: Adalaj's five-storey stepwell (1498) stays several degrees cooler than the surface — an early feat of climate design.

topics.title: Shore Temple, Mahabalipuram
topics.fact: The Pallavas carved Mahabalipuram's Shore Temple around 700 CE — one of the oldest stone temples in South India.

topics.title: Hoysaleswara Temple, Halebidu
topics.fact: Halebidu's Hoysaleswara Temple is covered in soapstone friezes so detailed you can count the beads on a dancer's necklace.

topics.title: Chennakeshava Temple, Belur
topics.fact: The Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana began Belur's Chennakeshava Temple in 1117 CE; it reportedly took 103 years to finish.

topics.title: Ranakpur Jain Temple
topics.fact: Ranakpur's 15th-century marble temple has 1,444 carved pillars — and no two are exactly alike.

topics.title: The Iron Pillar of Delhi
topics.fact: The Iron Pillar of Delhi has barely rusted in over 1,600 years, thanks to a protective phosphorus-rich iron layer.

topics.title: India and the Number Zero
topics.fact: Zero as a true number was formalised in India; the Bakhshali manuscript holds one of its oldest known dot-symbols.

topics.title: Aryabhata
topics.fact: In 476 CE Aryabhata pegged the year's length to within minutes and argued that the Earth spins on its axis.

topics.title: Sushruta, Father of Surgery
topics.fact: Roughly 2,500 years ago Sushruta described cataract removal and reconstructive plastic surgery in the Sushruta Samhita.

topics.title: Takshashila (Taxila)
topics.fact: Takshashila drew students from across Asia more than 2,000 years ago — one of the world's earliest centres of higher learning.

topics.title: Nalanda
topics.fact: Nalanda's library was so vast that, when the university was destroyed, it is said to have burned for months.

topics.title: Brahmagupta's Rules for Zero
topics.fact: In 628 CE Brahmagupta wrote the first known rules for calculating with zero and with negative numbers.

topics.title: Bhaskara II
topics.fact: In the 12th century Bhaskara II toyed with infinity and instantaneous change — ideas calculus would formalise 500 years later.

topics.title: Madhava & the Kerala School
topics.image_query: Kerala school of astronomy and mathematics
topics.fact: Around 1400, Madhava of Sangamagrama derived infinite series for pi and trigonometry — centuries before Newton and Leibniz.

topics.title: Varahamihira
topics.fact: Varahamihira's 6th-century Brihat Samhita packed astronomy, gemmology, architecture and even weather-reading into one encyclopedia.

topics.title: Jantar Mantar, Jaipur
topics.fact: Jaipur's Jantar Mantar (1734) is a park of giant masonry instruments, including the world's largest stone sundial.

topics.title: Wootz Steel
topics.fact: South Indian wootz steel was so prized that, forged into Damascus blades, its making was chased across the world.

topics.title: Kallanai (Grand Anicut)
topics.fact: The Chola-era Kallanai dam on the Kaveri has been diverting water to farmers for around 1,800 years — and still works.

topics.title: Panini's Grammar
topics.fact: Over 2,400 years ago Panini described Sanskrit with about 4,000 rules so precise they read almost like computer code.

topics.title: Charaka Samhita
topics.fact: The Charaka Samhita laid out diagnosis, ethics and treatment — a cornerstone of Ayurvedic medicine for two millennia.

topics.title: Lothal Dockyard
topics.fact: The Indus city of Lothal had a tidal dockyard around 2400 BCE — among the earliest known anywhere on Earth.

topics.title: Dholavira's Water System
topics.fact: The Harappan city of Dholavira survived a desert with a network of dams and reservoirs built about 4,500 years ago.

topics.title: The Indus Script
topics.fact: The Indus Valley left thousands of inscribed seals — a 4,000-year-old script no one has ever deciphered.

topics.title: The Chola Naval Empire
topics.fact: The Chola navy sailed across the Bay of Bengal to conquer parts of Southeast Asia — a rare Indian sea-power.

topics.title: Rajaraja Chola I
topics.fact: Rajaraja Chola I forged one of medieval history's great empires and commissioned the Brihadeeswarar Temple.

topics.title: Vijayanagara Empire
topics.fact: At its height Vijayanagara's capital was among the largest and richest cities on Earth.

topics.title: The Ahom Kingdom
topics.fact: The Ahom kingdom ruled Assam for about 600 years and repeatedly turned back Mughal invasions.

topics.title: The Maratha Empire
topics.fact: From the Deccan hills the Marathas rose to control much of the Indian subcontinent by the 18th century.

topics.title: Lachit Borphukan
topics.fact: In 1671 Lachit Borphukan's outnumbered Ahom navy shattered a Mughal fleet on the Brahmaputra at Saraighat.

topics.title: Ashoka the Great
topics.fact: After a bloody conquest of Kalinga, Emperor Ashoka renounced war and spread a message of tolerance carved onto stone pillars.

topics.title: Chandragupta Maurya
topics.fact: Guided by the strategist Chanakya, Chandragupta Maurya founded India's first great pan-Indian empire around 321 BCE.

topics.title: The Gupta Golden Age
topics.fact: Under the Guptas (4th to 6th century CE), Indian mathematics, astronomy, art and literature hit a legendary high point.

topics.title: Samudragupta
topics.fact: Samudragupta conquered so widely he has been called the 'Napoleon of India' — and he was a skilled musician too.

topics.title: Harshavardhana
topics.fact: Harsha united much of north India in the 7th century; the Chinese monk Xuanzang chronicled his tolerant court.

topics.title: The Pallavas
topics.fact: The Pallavas turned South Indian temple-building from wood and brick to enduring carved stone.

topics.title: The Pandyas
topics.fact: The ancient Pandya kingdom grew rich on pearls and traded with Rome from its capital at Madurai.

topics.title: The Rashtrakutas
topics.fact: The Rashtrakutas ruled the Deccan and commissioned the astonishing rock-cut Kailasa temple at Ellora.

topics.title: Shivaji and the Marathas
topics.fact: Shivaji built a kingdom on hill forts and swift guerrilla tactics, founding Maratha power in the 17th century.

topics.title: The Chalukyas of Badami
topics.fact: The Badami Chalukyas cut spectacular cave temples into red sandstone cliffs in the 6th century.

topics.title: The Kakatiyas
topics.fact: The Kakatiyas built the Ramappa temple on bricks so light they float on water — now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

topics.title: Krishnadevaraya
topics.fact: Krishnadevaraya, Vijayanagara's greatest king, was also a poet who wrote a celebrated Telugu epic.

topics.title: The Kumbh Mela
topics.fact: The Kumbh Mela is the largest human gathering on Earth — its crowds are visible from space.

topics.title: The Twelve Jyotirlingas
topics.fact: Twelve jyotirlingas across India mark shrines where Shiva is revered as an endless pillar of light.

topics.title: Ram Setu / Adam's Bridge
topics.fact: Ram Setu is a 48km chain of limestone shoals stretching between India and Sri Lanka.

topics.title: The Char Dham
topics.fact: The Char Dham — Badrinath, Dwarka, Puri and Rameswaram — mark four sacred corners of India for pilgrims.

topics.title: Kashi (Varanasi)
topics.fact: Varanasi is one of the world's oldest continuously lived-in cities, its ghats stepping down to the Ganga for millennia.

topics.title: Ramanathaswamy Temple
topics.fact: Rameswaram's Ramanathaswamy Temple has the longest pillared corridor of any temple in India.

topics.title: Amarnath Cave Shrine
topics.fact: High in the Himalayas, the Amarnath cave forms a natural ice lingam that waxes and wanes with the moon.

topics.title: Mount Kailash
topics.fact: Mount Kailash is revered across four religions — and though far lower than Everest, its summit has never been climbed.

topics.title: Jagannath & the Rath Yatra
topics.fact: Puri's Rath Yatra rolls deity chariots so massive that the English word 'juggernaut' came from them.

topics.title: Tirumala Tirupati
topics.fact: Tirumala's Venkateswara Temple is among the most visited pilgrimage sites on Earth, drawing tens of thousands daily.

topics.title: The Golden Temple
topics.fact: Amritsar's Golden Temple runs the world's largest free community kitchen, serving all comers every single day.

topics.title: Mahabodhi Temple, Bodh Gaya
topics.fact: At Bodh Gaya, a descendant of the very Bodhi tree marks where the Buddha is said to have found enlightenment.

topics.title: The Great Stupa of Sanchi
topics.fact: Sanchi's Great Stupa, begun under Ashoka, is ringed by carved gateways among the finest early Buddhist art.

topics.title: Dwarka
topics.fact: Off the coast of Dwarka, Krishna's legendary city, divers have mapped submerged stone structures.

topics.title: Kedarnath Temple
topics.fact: The stone Kedarnath temple has stood high in the Himalayas for centuries, surviving even the 2013 floods.

topics.title: Pushkar
topics.fact: Pushkar holds one of the very few temples dedicated to Brahma, beside a lake said to have formed from a lotus.

topics.title: Chola Bronzes
topics.fact: Chola lost-wax bronzes like the dancing Nataraja rank among the finest metal sculptures ever cast.

topics.title: The Ajanta Caves
topics.fact: Ajanta's 2,000-year-old cave paintings lay forgotten until a British hunting party stumbled on them in 1819.

topics.title: The Ellora Caves
topics.fact: Ellora's 34 rock-cut caves place Hindu, Buddhist and Jain monuments peacefully side by side.

topics.title: Nataraja, the Cosmic Dance
topics.fact: The Nataraja — Shiva dancing the universe into being — is so iconic that a statue of it stands outside CERN.

topics.title: Tanjore Painting
topics.fact: Thanjavur paintings glow with real gold leaf and once-set gemstones, a South Indian art centuries old.

topics.title: Madhubani Painting
topics.fact: Madhubani art, traditionally painted by women on mud walls, fills every gap with pattern and natural dye.

topics.title: Pattachitra
topics.fact: Odisha's Pattachitra scrolls are painted on cloth stiffened with tamarind paste, using only natural colours.

topics.title: Warli Art
topics.fact: Warli tribal art tells whole stories with just circles, triangles and lines in white rice paste.

topics.title: Mughal Miniatures
topics.fact: Mughal miniatures blended Persian and Indian styles into jewel-like scenes finer than a fingernail.

topics.title: Pahari & Kangra Painting
topics.fact: The Pahari painters of the Himalayan foothills gave Krishna's tales their tender, lyrical visual style.

topics.title: Gandhara Sculpture
topics.fact: Gandhara artists carved the Buddha in flowing Greek-style robes — a fusion born of Alexander's legacy.

topics.title: The Mathura School
topics.fact: Mathura's sculptors created some of the earliest Indian-made images of the Buddha, in warm red sandstone.

topics.title: The Amaravati Marbles
topics.fact: The Amaravati stupa's limestone reliefs are among the finest narrative carvings of the ancient world.

topics.title: The Dancing Girl of Mohenjo-daro
topics.fact: The 'Dancing Girl' is a 4,500-year-old bronze, lost-wax cast by Indus craftsmen with startling confidence.

topics.title: Bhimbetka Rock Art
topics.fact: The Bhimbetka shelters hold prehistoric paintings, some from the Mesolithic around 10,000 years ago.

topics.title: The Elephanta Caves
topics.fact: In a cave on an island near Mumbai, a three-faced Shiva (Trimurti) has gazed out in stone since the 6th century.

topics.title: Gomateshwara, Shravanabelagola
topics.fact: The roughly 17m Gomateshwara statue is carved from a single stone and ceremonially bathed once every 12 years.
